title: Hindu Gods & Greek Gods | Shocking Similarities Explained
tags: similarities between greek and hindu gods
similarities between Hindu and Greek gods
description:
Why do so many gods from different cultures look the same? Why does Zeus remind us of Indra, Ra of Shiva, Hermes of Narada, or Aphrodite of Lakshmi? In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we continue the series on the evolution of gods and religions and trace how myths travelled, changed, and merged across civilizations,

From Egyptian Ra, Horus, and Osiris, to Greek Zeus, Poseidon, and Hermes, to Hindu Shiva, Vishnu, and Indra, we see uncanny similarities. Gods of thunder, gods of love, gods of death, and messenger gods keep reappearing — only slightly modified for local cultures. The Trinity concept appears in Egypt, Greece, Christianity, and Hinduism. Even Zoroastrian Ahuras and Daevas sound strikingly like Hindu Asuras and Devas — just reversed.

These parallels show that religions evolved like living species — branching, mutating, and adapting as humans migrated. Just like Darwin’s evolution, stories evolved too. Whether it’s Zeus turning into Shiva, Hermes into Narada, or Aphrodite into Lakshmi, myths carried cultural DNA across continents.

We also bust the idea that any single religion “came first.” Just like claiming Jack & Rose from Titanic were historical because the ship existed, claiming myths as fact is flawed. Stories don’t prove reality — evidence does.

If you’ve searched for origin of gods, evolution of religions, similarities between gods, Ra vs Shiva, Zeus vs Indra, Hermes vs Narada, Aphrodite vs Lakshmi, Asuras vs Devas, Zoroastrianism influence, or Pale Blue Thoughts, this video lays out the fascinating story.

Attributing any gods to a spread of culture between places like Egypt and Greece or any other group is a very limited view. Many of these cultures were seeing the similarities between their own cultures and ones in new lands when they first arrived. The similarities are largely because religion probably formed in the area around modern Ukraine before Indo-Europeans split out of the region into as far as the Atlantic Ocean and India. Then the rest of the similarities happened from cross-pollination of ideas. But, for example, it's basic thinking to say the Roman Gods came from the Greek Gods, etc. The Romans already had their own gods and merely adapted around the more developed Greek influence. Very much the same with Indian religion, where Greeks merely influenced things and did not originate them.
